changes: Confirmed weights (0.7 kg cock, 0.6 kg hen): Wikipedia gives 700 g and 600 g, Star Milling 24 oz and 21 oz, and Poultrykeeper 680 to 790 g and 570 to 680 g for the British Belgian bantam standard. Origin Belgium confirmed by all three. Added temperament friendly from Star Milling. Egg color creamy white and small egg size rest on Wikipedia; Poultrykeeper's group page says tinted, which is compatible. Note: breeds.json stores the raw weights as 700 and 600 in the kg columns (grams), not a breeds_extra field, so not changed here.

summary.value: The Barbu d'Anvers is a tiny Belgian chicken that exists only as a bantam, with no large version. It ranks among the oldest bantams anywhere and is linked to the Antwerp area, where small bearded fowl were kept for centuries. The name means bearded bird of Antwerp, and a thick muff of feathers hides the earlobes. It stands upright, pushes a round chest forward, carries an arched tail, and wears a small rose comb on clean legs. Cocks weigh about 1.5 pounds and hens a little over 1.3 pounds. Belgium recognizes dozens of color patterns, including quail, porcelain and cuckoo. Hens lay small cream colored eggs and make good sitters and mothers. The birds are friendly and do well as pets, especially with room to roam, but most keepers raise them for shows. It remains the most secure of the Belgian bantam breeds.
